topic.title: URL media and game packs in AltirraSDL
topic.p: Use Open Image from URL for a single image you want to open or boot now. Use Add from URL in Game Library to keep a game or a large ZIP collection in your library without booting it.
topic.h2: Open or boot a single image

ol.li: Choose File > Open Image from URL. In gaming/mobile mode use Load Game > From URL.
Paste a direct HTTP or HTTPS file link, rather than a web page containing a download button.
Choose Open Image to attach through the normal open workflow, or Boot Image to load, reset and run through the normal boot workflow.

topic.p: This path limits downloads and individual expanded archive members to 64 MiB. Compressed-media preflight also limits aggregate expansion to 128 MiB, ZIP entries to 4096 and nested compression to four levels. ZIP and gzip files go through the existing media loader; opening a ZIP normally selects its first supported image.

Cancel Download or closing this dialog cancels the pending transfer. Download failures and cancellation preserve mounted media and running/paused state. Normal image parsing, cartridge mapper selection and compatibility handling follow download completion.
topic.h2: Add games or large ZIP packs to Game Library

ol.li: Open Game Library and Add from URL.
Expand Download location and choose a folder on a drive with enough free space. The default is library-downloads/ below the Altirra configuration directory.

Paste a direct game-file or ZIP-pack URL, then select Import. ZIP downloads stream to disk and can be multiple gigabytes; the single-image 64 MiB download limit does not apply to the whole pack. The importer looks for supported game members of 64 MiB or less.
After completion the archive/file is added as a library source and scanned. Choose a game from the library when you want to play it. Import does not boot or replace mounted media.

topic.p: Packs stay intact as archives; member paths are not extracted onto the host filesystem. A progress bar appears when the server supplies a total size, and the dialog shows received bytes. Hide or closing the import window leaves the transfer running; reopen Add from URL to see it. Cancel Import explicitly cancels. Incomplete staging files are removed after cancellation/failure.

Downloads use content-derived storage names to avoid overwriting another import. Removing a source from the library leaves its downloaded file on disk. Keep the destination available while using that source; moving/deleting the file breaks that source until you update it. The destination choice persists across restarts.

ul.li: HTML/web-page error: copy the direct file URL. A repository page, login page or download landing page is not an Atari image.
Single-image size limit: use Game Library's importer for a large ZIP collection. It is a separate workflow, not a larger boot-image limit.
No games found: the ZIP must contain supported media files. At least one supported game member of 64 MiB or less must be present.
Write/disk-full error: choose a writable destination with enough space for the entire downloaded pack. The importer does not expand all members onto disk.
HTTPS/certificate error: check the computer's date, network/proxy configuration and system certificate store. Verification stays enabled.
Backend unavailable: Linux/macOS require the host libcurl library. Windows uses WinHTTP; Android uses Java HTTP connections. Browser builds retain their existing browser game-pack workflow.

topic.p: Single-image downloads remain in downloads/ below the configuration directory. Library imports use their chosen destination instead. Neither store is automatically evicted; remove files only after they are no longer mounted or needed by library sources, profiles or recent-image entries.
